definition: Kruskal's algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by considering edges from lightest to heaviest and keeping an edge when its endpoints are not already connected. Union-find answers that connection test. Skipping an edge that would close a cycle is what keeps the result a tree.

complexity.time: O(E log E) to sort the edges, which dominates the nearly constant union-find operations.

examples: Laying cable by always adding the cheapest link that joins two separate sites
